deleted_superseded_comments.original_text: A penniless prisoner mailed the Supreme Court a handwritten letter — and won 9–0. Should the right to a lawyer depend on a county's budget?
Police broke into Dollree Mapp's home without a real warrant — and the evidence was thrown out. Was that trade-off worth it?
The detail that made this story click: ordinary customers could not go negative, but Alameda had a special exception. What other financial stories should get this treatment?
An officer can stop you and pat you down with no warrant — just "reasonable suspicion" that something's off. Where should the line sit between keeping the street safe and your right to be left alone?
